findings.claim: With six cars every race started from RACE/RETRY/NEXT RACE ends on a 6-row results screen that does not fit the 844×390 phone viewport. The content needs about 491px in a 357px box, is centred so it is clipped at both ends, and the page cannot scroll. RETRY and NEXT RACE start at y≈385 of 390, a sliver of about 5px, and pause is disabled after the finish, so a phone player cannot leave the results screen.
findings.evidence: Reference viewport 844×390. results-screen.ts:62-73 stacks [stripes+label+title] / [roundel+best chip | table] / [RETRY, NEXT RACE] in one column. .ui-screen centres it (screens.css:3-7). html, body have overflow:hidden; touch-action:none (base.css:2-13), so nothing scrolls. A row is .ui-value 28px + 2×4 padding + 2×3 border = 42px with 8px gaps (results.css:67-77). Six rows make a 330px table (header and gap included). Column = 77 (title block) + 16 + 330 + 16 + 52 (button) = 491px, versus 390 − 12 (--safe-top) − 21 (--safe-bottom) = 357px. About 134px overflows, split over both ends. Screenshot screenshots/844x390/stage/results--podium.png (6 racers): 'BRAMBLE BENDS' is cut at the top, stripes and label are above y=0, and the buttons' tops are at y≈385. With 2 racers (race/bends-finished.png) the buttons sit at y≈303–355 and everything fits. The mockup guardrails/design/mockups/S5-results.png fits 6 rows plus both buttons in 844×390. The gate race screenshots only show 2 rows because the protected driver starts 2-car races. Before B04 a real race had 2 rows; now every one has 6. Pause is ignored once the player has finished (game.ts:166). The spec play-test steps 5-6 ('tap RETRY, then NEXT RACE') cannot be done on a phone. The AC7 UI test passes only because happy-dom has no layout.
findings.suggestedFix: Lay the screen out as in mockup S5, in results-screen.ts and results.css. Put the stripes full width on top. Put label, track name, roundel and best-lap chip in the left column. Put the table and then the RETRY / NEXT RACE row in the right column. Make rows about 32-36px (type at --type-button-size, tighter row padding and gap, tokens only) so that 6 rows + header + buttons fit the 357px content box. Scrolling is not an option because body is overflow:hidden and touch-action:none.

findings.claim: startRace() sets menuTrack before raceDrivers() can throw on an invalid carCount. A rejected call therefore still switches the track that the RACE button and the next startRace() use, and that GameState.trackId reports.
findings.evidence: game.ts:236-238: `const track = getTrack(options.trackId ?? menuTrack.id); menuTrack = track; const drivers = raceDrivers(options.carCount ?? DEFAULT_CAR_COUNT);`. raceDrivers throws 'a race has 1..6 cars, got 7' for carCount 7, 0 or 2.5 (src/content/drivers.ts:25-27). Steps: createGame (menu, menuTrack = TRACKS[0] = bends, because tracks are sorted by file name). Then `expect(() => game.startRace({ trackId: 'dust-bowl', carCount: 7 })).toThrow()` passes, and `game.state().trackId` is now 'dust-bowl' (was 'bends'). No race started and the start screen still says Bramble Bends, yet game.startRace() and the RACE button now start Dust Bowl. Before this diff carCount was the constant DRIVERS.length, so nothing after `menuTrack = track` could fail on input; the new throw point is introduced here.
findings.suggestedFix: Move `menuTrack = track;` below the raceDrivers(...) and createWorld(...) calls, just before `race = {`, so a failed start leaves the menu state untouched.

findings.claim: The start screen subtitle is built once at createGame from the initial menuTrack, but menuTrack changes on every startRace (NEXT RACE moves to the next track). After NEXT RACE → QUIT TO MENU the start screen still shows the old track name and lap count while RACE starts the new track. This predates B04, but sits in the createStartScreen options literal whose onRace line this diff edits.
findings.evidence: game.ts:137-140: `createStartScreen(menuLayer, { onRace: () => game.startRace({ trackId: menuTrack.id, carCount: PLAYER_CAR_COUNT }), subtitle: `${menuTrack.name} · ${menuTrack.laps} laps` })`. The subtitle is a string evaluated once; showMenu() (game.ts:264-268) only calls startScreen.show() and never refreshes it. src/ui/start-screen.ts renders the text once and exposes no setter. Steps: boot, subtitle 'Bramble Bends · 2 laps' (TRACKS[0] = bends). RACE, finish, NEXT RACE (nextTrackId gives dust-bowl, menuTrack = dust-bowl). Pause, QUIT TO MENU. The start screen still reads 'Bramble Bends · 2 laps'; pressing RACE starts Dust Bowl, 3 laps. Test: `game.startRace({ trackId: 'dust-bowl', seed: 1 }); game.showMenu(); expect(root.querySelector('.ui-start__subtitle')?.textContent).toBe('Dust Bowl · 3 laps')` fails (still 'Bramble Bends · 2 laps').
findings.suggestedFix: Let the start screen update its subtitle: make createStartScreen always render the subtitle node and return setSubtitle(text), then call it from showMenu() with the current menuTrack. Use the singular 'lap' for 1 lap, as results-screen.ts:106 does.

checked.target: src/sim/world.ts createWorld: determinism and existing replays
checked.how: Read the full diff. The RNG draws per slot are still back then side (2 per slot, same order). For i<4 the column/side/createCar expressions are unchanged, so worlds with ≤4 cars are bit-identical. The only new sim import is the pure sampleAt. Gates G2/G3 pass (+0.0%, 5 replays). Grep: no createWorld caller with carCount>4 in tests, harness or gates.

checked.target: src/sim/world.ts curved slots (i≥4): geometry for all seeds, not only 1-20
checked.how: Hand-computed worst-case jitter: lateral ≤ 1.5+0.4 = 1.9 vs halfWidth 4.2/5.5; consecutive rows ≥ 4.8 apart along the track. Prop clearance on bends, left hay-bale row at lateral −6.2 (bound 1.17), is 4.3−1.17 = 3.13 > 3 at the worst jitter. Dust Bowl right tyre stacks sit at +7. Side convention (cos h, sin h) matches buildTrack's prop placement. No seed-dependent failure found.

checked.target: src/game.ts tick(), Race.inputs, bots[i] ↔ car i+1
checked.how: Traced one tick: inputs[0] is the player or NO_INPUT after the finish; bots[i].input(world) is called once per tick before stepWorld, in the same order as the twin world in the tests. stepWorld copies inputs into the module scratch `clean`, so the shared NO_INPUT object and reused array are never mutated. carCount=1 gives bots=[] and one input, which is fine.

Traced driver 2-car → UI 6-car on the same track: the key differs, so dispose plus create. Same key: reset() reuses the scene. raceDrivers(n) is always the first n drivers, so length is a sufficient key. The dust pool's per-car arrays only grow. Old scene reference is replaced before any frame runs.

checked.target: startRace / RETRY / RESTART RACE / NEXT RACE / QUIT TO MENU state reset
checked.how: Walked each path: ui.reset rebuilds HudState, minimap dots (fresh outline array each race → rebuild), lastStep, lapsSeen, finishShown, and hides results, countdown and pause. paused=false, input.reset(), startLoop() resets lastFrame/accumulator after a pause. Fresh bots per race, so no stuck/reverse counters leak. No stale view model found, other than F3.

checked.target: src/ui/results-screen.ts with 6 racers: order, gap, ties, late finishers
checked.how: order = position then car index; leader is finished because finished cars rank first and the screen opens on the player's finish; formatGap regex gives +1.08 / +10.50 / +1:05.00. Rows are rebuilt per show(); update() re-renders on any finishTick or position change; the roundel can only move down after the player's finish. Names and numbers are index-aligned from drivers.

rebuild() creates one circle per car (player radius 5 vs 4), appends the player's circle last (findIndex guarded for no player), and the dots array stays in car order. CSS classes exist for all six body colours; navy gets a cream ring. POS denominator comes from colours.length.

checked.target: Input paths: touch hit-test under the results overlay, keyboard, Esc
checked.how: input/touch.ts calls preventDefault on pointerdown, which does not suppress click, so RETRY/NEXT RACE still fire even over touch zones. Zones are disabled only while paused, which is harmless because tick() ignores player input after the finish. Esc after the finish is ignored by setPaused. No gas-key path activates the focused NEXT RACE button.

checked.target: Listeners, timers and rAF added by the diff
checked.how: The diff adds none. The existing window resize and visibilitychange listeners in createGame exist once per game and are never removed, which is a standing design with a single game per page. rafId handling is unchanged: stopLoop/startLoop pair around pause and startRace.

checked.target: src/sim purity (no Math.random, Date, clock, render state)
checked.how: The diff touches src/sim only in world.ts (sampleAt import, grid branch). Dust RNG is the render-side seeded createRng. tests/sim/purity.test.ts passes per gates.

Read rng.ts (mulberry32) and bot.ts: stream seed = imul(seed, 0x9e3779b1) + carIndex. Adjacent seeds give well-mixed offset and pace, so per-car variation holds and runs are reproducible. Bots only read world and keep per-bot slowTicks/reverseTicks.

checked.target: Existing tests that rely on the 2-car default (pause-results, results-drivers, pause tests)
checked.how: They call startRace() without carCount, so they still get 2 cars. Their RETRY/NEXT RACE steps now start 6-car races, but they only compare fresh-race snapshots that are equal on both paths, and gates pass 598/598.

src/driver/index.ts calls startRace({trackId, seed}), so it stays at 2 cars; harness/screens/capture.ts and g2-measure.ts use CARS=2. Gates therefore never exercise 6 cars, as the plan audit notes. This is why the F1 overflow shows only in the 6-racer stage screenshot, not in the race screenshots.

checked.target: Camera, scene.update and render for 6 liveries
checked.how: Read scene.ts, camera.ts, car.ts and dust.ts: update() loops cars.length, the camera follows playerIndex 0, and car names are unique ('car:player', 'car:7'…). All five AI liveries pass validateLivery (AI body from the list, never red, stripe ≠ body). Dust capacity 48 recycles puffs and is not a correctness issue.

Read both files: every AC has a test named 'AC<n>:' in a new file. The state() copies avoid aliasing in AC4. Twin-world input recording matches how game.play replays inputs. No .skip/.only/@ts-ignore. Test strength is R5's lane, so I did not analyse mutation coverage.

checked.target: Spec play-test claims vs the camera frame
checked.how: Camera frame is 56 units wide, so slot 4 (30 back) and slot 5 (36 back) sit at or beyond the left screen edge at GO. This affects the play-test step 'five cars lined up behind you' (R1's lane), so I did not file it as an R2 finding.
